newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end firmer on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end firmer on selective buying.

text.p: Selective buying lifted Kuala Lumpur share prices to a stronger finish, with secondary stocks holding a narrow edge over main board issues.

Continuing a firmer trend from earlier in the day, the Composite Index ended up 9.14 points or 0.77 percent to 1,201.03. The Second Board index turned stronger during the afternoon, gaining 4.83 points or 0.91 percent to 532.74.

Blue chips like United Engineers attracted interest, said an institutional dealer at a large brokerage firm. "There's always room for rebound," he added, referring to the Second Board which has been correcting in the past few weeks.
Turnover was about even with Wednesday, at over 126 million shares. Winners outpaced losers by 346 to 210.
"Currently, the market is forming a flag formation," said a technical analyst at a local research firm. "It's a consolidating pattern, basically. To me, the upside remains intact."
He sees the Composite Index trading between 1,180 to 1,220 over the next few weeks.
"The low volume is a positive sign. Because the market has retraced downwards on low volume, that means investors are just staying sidelined rather than selling off," he added.
